sources.excerpt: OKKO FX Holy Grit Fuzz | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit OKKO FX Holy Grit Fuzz Updated Oct. 3, 2022 | by Paolo De Gregorio Built by hand in Germany, the OKKO FX Holy Grit is an original circuit vaguely inspired by vintage fuzzes like the Fuzz Face and Tone Bender that can produce a variety of tones from gritty overdrive to low gain fuzz or vintage preamp. Rather than faithfully recreating the tones of those units, the Holy Grit is a modern pedal that complements their raw and complex texture with the clarity and dynamic response of the best overdrives. Employing a set of matched low gain silicon transistors, the Holy Grit is voiced between germanium warmth and silicon presence, and features a pre-gain Bass knob and a post-gain Treble one. A BIAS toggle selects one of three bias settings (individually set for each pedal): • UP = high headroom setting, least amount of fuzz and compression, tight and precise • MIDDLE = the “almost too low“ bias – dirty, buzzy, can get into velcro fuzz territory… fun! • DOWN = “the golden middle“ There’s also a Buffer toggle on the back side of the case that allows you to make the circuit unbuffered for a more resonant tone and better cleanup, although the pedal needs to be first in the chain. Take a listen to the OKKO FX Holy Grit in the video below. OKKO FX Holy Grit, Builder’s Notes Gritty overdrive, low gain fuzz, vintage preamp – no matter how you call it, the Holy Grit combines the clarity and dynamic response of a great overdrive with the raw and complex texture of a vintage fuzz. The intuitive controls let you dial in anything from cleanish boost with a little grit to full-blown vintage „amp on 11“ sounds. Plug it into a clean or driven amp, stack with boosters, overdrives or fuzz pedals, Holy Grit will deliver – for guitar, bass, keys or whatever you want to spice up. The circuit is based on the classic Fuzz Face/Tone Bender but heavily tweaked into something else. We’re using a set of matched low gain silicon transistors here (parts numbers may differ from one unit to another), voiced between germanium warmth and silicon presence. Controls: FUZZ… well, you know. Level of distortion. Set low for boosting overdriven amps or dirt pedals and work your way up to see how far you can go. LEVEL, as expected, controls the output volume. Plenty of volume on tap, even with the Fuzz knob set to minimum. BASS is a pregain control so more bass = more fuzz. Play with it and you’ll find the perfect balance between tight/precise and bold/buzzy. TREBLE rolls off highs post gain at variable frequencies. BIAS TOGGLE selects one of three bias settings (individually set for each pedal): – UP = high headroom setting, least amount of fuzz and compression, tight and precise – MIDDLE = the „almost too low“ bias – dirty, buzzy, can get into velcro fuzz territory… fun! – DOWN = „the golden middle“ BUFFER TOGGLE UP = buffered mode. Don’t worry about the placement in your signal chain, just activate the HG’s special buffer and you’re set. Gives a little extra edge and presence in the mix compared to DOWN = unbuffered mode. If you prefer the classic way, just connect your guitar straight to the HG without the buffer. Slightly darker, more resonant tone, better cleanup with the guitar volume. sources.excerpt: --> OKKO FX Holy Grit Demo Review | Loopy Demos Show or hide the side bar navigation Loopy Demos Demos Posts Manufacturers About Contact Demos Posts Manufacturers About Contact All demos OKKO FX Holy Grit Jun 1, 2022 Read next Budget Guitar Pedals That Sound Expensive: Best Value Effects Under $150 The Holy Grit by OKKO FX is a Fuzz Face/Tone Bender-inspired dirt box that refuses to stay in one lane. Built by hand in Leipzig since 2003, it runs from a clean boost all the way through woody breakup and into full-on cranked-tweed fuzz. The circuit uses matched low-gain silicon transistors, and the result sits closer to an overdriven amp than a pedal clanging against a clean signal. I kept reaching for it when I wanted body and character rather than just a blanket of gain. Controls The panel puts Fuzz and Level in the top row, with Bass and Treble below flanking a centre Bias toggle. That toggle is the personality control: up is high headroom, clean and precise; middle is slightly underbiased, buzzy and hairy; down is medium gain, a bit thicker. In the demo I’ve set up sweeps for the Fuzz Knob, Bass Knob, Treble Knob, and Bias Toggle so you can hear what each one does. Bass is a pre-gain control, so dialing it up pushes more signal into the gain stage and raises the fuzz intensity. Treble is post-gain, rolling off brightness after the dirt happens. Neither has a huge range, which I think is intentional. You can’t really dial in a bad sound. Level has a lot of headroom, with unity around 10 o’clock, leaving the upper half for clean boosting or front-end smashing. A buffer toggle on the top face lets you place the pedal anywhere in a chain without the usual fuzz-face impedance headaches. Everything here was recorded buffered, since unbuffered mode needs real pickups at the input, which my reamping setup can’t replicate. How It Sounds The Cranked Tweed preset is the most characterful spot on the pedal: Fuzz maxed, Bias in the middle position. The whole thing gets that loose, harmonically complex voice of a tweed amp hitting its limits, which is the preset I kept coming back to for Neil Young-ish open chords. Light Breakup pulls back the Fuzz and lifts the Bias to the high-headroom position. The grit thins out to something closer to a slightly pushed amp, still defined and responsive. Sweet Fuzz goes the other direction: Fuzz and Bass both maxed, Bias in the low position. That stacks the pre-gain bass boost against the lower bias and you get into properly saturated fuzz territory. The Boost preset zeroes the Fuzz knob entirely and cranks Level and Treble. With Fuzz at zero the circuit runs nearly clean and the output becomes a bright, punchy boost. It also works well on bass, where the pre-gain Bass control and amp-like voicing translate without getting woolly. Holy Grit vs Keeley Fuzz Bender Both pedals are rooted in Tone Bender topology and both offer more flexibility than a classic two-knob fuzz. The Keeley Fuzz Bender adds a three-band EQ and a dry Blend control, which makes it easier to dial in extreme gated velcro sounds while keeping low-end definition. The Holy Grit has no dry blend, but the Bias toggle and pre-gain Bass control let you shape the character of the saturation itself rather than sculpting around it. The Fuzz Bender leans more modern and surgical; the Holy Grit leans more analog and amp-like. Who It’s For Players who love the idea of a fuzz but find most fuzzes too one-dimensional will get a lot out of this. It suits classic rock, country, and blues, works well after a buffer or anywhere in a modern pedalboard, and the bass guitar use case is real. If you need extreme gated tones or a very distinct fuzz-as-effect character, the Holy Grit stays on the warmer, amp-like side. It also doesn’t do modulated or synth-like fuzz. But for everything in the boost-to-cranked-tweed range, it covers a lot of ground without ever sounding forced. Specs Circuit: Fuzz Face/Tone Bender topology, heavily modified; matched low-gain si
